title: The Porch Light Rule
concept: Every house on Linden Row leaves its porch light on all night. A new tenant turns hers off and learns why the street keeps the light burning.
setting: A quiet cul-de-sac at 2 a.m.; every porch lit except one.
conflict: Nadia thinks the rule is superstition and an electricity waste.
escalation: After she switches it off, porch lights down the street go dark one by one, moving toward her house.
reveal: The lights aren't protection for the residents — they mark houses that are already 'taken'. Hers was the only one still safe.
ending: Nadia reaches for the switch to turn it back on. Her finger stops. Something on the other side of the door turns it on for her.
emotional_objective: Dread built from a mundane rule, then a cold inversion.

hooks.line: On my street, you never turn off the porch light. I found out why on my first night.
hooks.first_visual: A row of lit porches; one goes dark.

hooks.line: I turned off my porch light at 2 a.m. The whole street noticed.
hooks.first_visual: Finger on a switch, click, darkness.

hooks.line: The lights on my street are going out one by one. Mine is next.
hooks.first_visual: Overhead shot: lights blinking off toward camera.

hooks.line: My neighbour left a note: 'Keep it on. Please. Not for you.'
hooks.first_visual: A shaky handwritten note taped to a door.

hooks.line: Why is mine the only house on the street with the light off?
hooks.first_visual: Wide shot: one dark house among glowing porches.

originality_review: Original premise. Avoids known 'rules' creepypasta structures by inverting the purpose of the rule; no borrowed characters or text.
